incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - routing anomaly detected: sudden spike of requests for tenant `acme-corp` being routed to Dedicated pool d-pool-42 (intended to be Hosted). Increased 5xx/504 errors observed from 03:04:12 UTC. Pager fired.

pagerduty: Paging oncall @oncall-erin (escalation policy: incidents->SRE primary).

oncall-erin: acked — looking now. any idea if this is a config push?

Ben (eng-sre): grabbing logs. At first glance we have high reject rates from dedicated instances (OOM/reject) and the routing layer shows a policy evaluation hit where tenant match returned `tier: dedicated` even though tenant is marked hosted.

Carlos (eng-runtime): I can see the routing decision trace: `route_eval -> rule_set v3.7.2` applied at 03:04:09 — that rule set was updated earlier today by ops. Looks like precedence order changed. Snippet:

```
# rule_set v3.7.2 (applied 2026-03-15T03:04:08Z)
- match: tenant == /acme-.*/
  action: assign_tier: dedicated
  priority: 50
- match: tenant == /acme-corp/
  action: assign_tier: hosted
  priority: 40
```

Carlos (eng-runtime): The generic acme-* rule has higher priority than the explicit acme-corp rule — that’s the bug. The intended behavior is explicit match first. Looks like the priority inversion happened during refactor of the rule compiler (PR #5482).

Maya (sre-lead): Confirmed impact: requests from acme-corp routed to dedicated pool which is currently near capacity -> constant fallback loops to region replicas -> timeouts. Customer facing: elevated 5xx and slow responses.

Diane (support): Diane here — acme-corp reported spike in errors ~03:08 UTC via support ticket. They had a production job running at the time. Flagging as high-severity.

Emily (customer-success): On call with customer contact; they want ETA and if data was exposed (they're asking about tenant isolation). I told them we're investigating routing only, no data plane keys seen in logs.

Ben (eng-sre): Mitigation plan: 1) Stop further rule propagation. 2) Temporarily pin acme-corp to hosted via an emergency override. 3) Scale dedicated pool to reduce 5xx while fix rolls.

Carlos (eng-runtime): I can push emergency override now: `redwoodctl routing override create --tenant acme-corp --tier hosted --expires 1h --reason \"emergency isolate\"`

oncall-erin: please execute and confirm.

Carlos (eng-runtime): done. Command output: `override id=ov-20260315-01 applied`. Routing traces after override show decisions going to hosted.

Ben (eng-sre): Applying a quick hotfix to rule_set to reorder priorities while we roll back the faulty compiler change. Rolling back PR #5482 to v3.7.1.

Carlos (eng-runtime): rollback applied, rule_set reverted to v3.7.1 (applied 03:15:02Z). No more precedence inversion in traces.

Maya (sre-lead): Observability: 5xx rate for acme-corp peaked at 12% of requests, total requests affected ~14k over 18 minutes. Latency normalized ~03:17 UTC after override + rollback. Marking initial mitigation success.

Diane (support): Customer informed of mitigation and asked for root cause and timeline for permanent fix.

Frank (product): Need to check client-side model variant mismatch too — any chance the dedicated pool had different model variant causing rejects?

Carlos (eng-runtime): Good catch — dedicated had model variant v1.8-quant while hosted runs v1.8 (float). But mismatched variants would not cause route decision; but they could explain some inference-level errors. After routing correction, we see a small tail of model errors (2%) that are internal inference failures — probably quantized kernel mismatch on older GPU drivers. We'll add a model-compat check to routing.

Ben (eng-sre): Actions taken summary: `override` pinned tenant -> trafffic restored to hosted; rolled rule_set back to v3.7.1; scaled dedicated pool to absorb in-flight; monitoring continues.

Maya (sre-lead): Who is taking next-phase ownership for full RCA and customer postmortem?

Ben (eng-sre): I'll lead the RCA with Carlos and runtime. Will include timeline, PR #5482 analysis, and steps to prevent recurrence (policy unit tests + CI gating).

Emily (customer-success): I'll draft customer-facing post-incident note, need estimated MTR and whether any data isolation breach — current status: no indication of data exfiltration.

Diane (support): Adding to ticket: affected window 03:04:09 - 03:22:00 UTC; degraded behaviors: 5xx/504 and slow startup errors.

Carlos (eng-runtime): Follow-ups I'm doing: 1) add model-compatibility check into route validator, 2) add policy precedence unit test cases (explicit > wildcard), 3) add CI gate rejecting rule_set publishes without canary on prod.

Ben (eng-sre): Also adding an alert rule: if `route_eval` shows unexpected tier assignment frequency > 1% for a tenant in a 5m window, fire fast.

Maya (sre-lead): Handoff: Ben/Carlos take post-incident; I'm unassigned from pager. oncall-erin, you can clear your page once you confirm no residual errors.

oncall-erin: confirming metrics stable for 10m. clearing page.

incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 2026-03-15T03:22:00Z. Root cause: rule compiler PR #5482 introduced priority inversion for wildcard vs explicit tenant rules, causing hosted tenants to be misassigned to dedicated tier. Secondary contributor: dedicated pool model variant differences increased error surface.

Frank (product): Proposed product follow-up: policy publish UI should show effective order preview and warn on priority collisions.

Ben (eng-sre): Postmortem owners: Ben, Carlos. ETA for postmortem draft: 2026-03-17 EOD. Will include remediation tickets: (1) enforce policy unit tests, (2) model-compat check, (3) canary publishes, (4) alert tuning.

Emily (customer-success): I'll share a customer note early tomorrow with timeline + mitigation steps.

Maya (sre-lead): Thanks team. Adding `postmortem` label and will schedule blameless review.

Diane (support): closing related support ticket after customer ack. :white_check_mark:

Ben (eng-sre): FYI saved commands used in incident runbook: `redwoodctl routing override create`, `redwoodctl rules rollback --to v3.7.1`, `redwoodctl pool scale d-pool-42 +6` — add to runbook after RCA.

Carlos (eng-runtime): Leaving a note: if we see similar, prefer override -> rollback -> scale order to minimize double routing flips.

incident-bot: follow-up tasks created: TASK-4521 (policy tests), TASK-4522 (model-compat validator), TASK-4523 (canary gating), assigned to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
